anomaly_def.Name: Database Memory Allocation Anomaly + Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly + CPU Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Database Memory Allocation Anomaly : Excessive growth of buffer caches, work areas, plan caches, and other engine heaps pushes total memory and swap usage beyond the safe capacity of the host, provoking paging, OOM events, or node eviction.
Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly : Concurrent sessions repeatedly serialize on hot buffer pages, latches, and I/O slots, producing buffer-busy and page-latch waits, prolonged pin times, and CPU spin while the desired pages are locked or in flight.
CPU Resource Anomaly : Database processes drive sustained host-CPU saturation, inflating run-queue depth, context switches, and scheduler wait events and degrading response time across the workload.

When these three root causes manifest together, the system exhibits a cascade of reinforcing symptoms: memory consumption climbs toward or beyond physical limits while latch hot-spots force threads to spin, collectively driving CPU utilization to 100 %. Operators observe simultaneous surges in buffer-busy/page-latch waits, soaring run-queue lengths, and erratic latency. Swapping or NUMA rebalancing lengthens latch hold times, which in turn amplifies CPU spin and further inflates the resident-set size as threads pin additional pages. Checkpoint and background flush activity may fall behind, yielding more dirty pages held in memory, while foreground queries stall on both CPU and buffer availability, making it difficult to isolate a single dominant bottleneck.

Causally, aggressive memory allocation shrinks free RAM, increasing the likelihood of paging and slowing latch acquisition paths that rely on fast memory access. Prolonged latching forces worker threads into tight spin loops, directly escalating CPU demand and starving other tasks. The resulting CPU saturation lengthens background flushing and eviction tasks, delaying reuse of buffer frames and intensifying buffer cache churn, which drives yet more memory growth. This positive feedback loop of memory pressure → latch contention → CPU exhaustion → slower memory reclamation locks the engine in a self-reinforcing spiral that can culminate in severe throughput collapse or instance termination.

entry.official_description: Fatal error: OOM while initializing time zones
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with a general engine-level execution problem surfaced by the official error catalogue, but its precise trigger must be interpreted together with workload context and surrounding evidence.
entry.solution_guidance: Review the surrounding workload, official description, and engine state to determine whether the issue is rooted in SQL logic, resource pressure, configuration, or environmental instability.
